Use this workflow to partition a planar Palace EPR parent by distance from its
original boundary and inspect the six returned band totals. The workflow uses
the geometry plan and one completed Palace EPR result.

✅ The geometry handoff and official Palace 0.18.1 preflight completed.

⏳ Q2D follow-up is paused. A Q2D result is not an input to this Palace-only
band workflow.

⏳ A complete Palace EPR return with six band totals is pending.

## Build the geometry bands

1. Build the normal source-backed `GeometryPlan`, including its original Nets
   and vacuum region. Call `snapshot0 = plan.prepare()` once, then use its
   detached `snapshot0.geometry_input` and `snapshot0.stack`.
2. Call `interpret_physical_geometry(...)` on those inputs. Pass its effective
   input and representation context to `build_route_construction_plan(...)`,
   then build the catalogue with `surface_distance_band_catalogue(...)`.
3. Inspect the unbanded catalogue and select a real parent and source-entity
   owner. For each catalogue row, find the matching
   `construction.surfaces` record by `parent_surface_id`; its
   `metadata.face_kind` supplies the `field_side` used by the result. Physical
   contribution side is recorded separately in
   `metadata.source_provenance.surface_contribution_ledger[*].side`.
   Treat these as distinct selections and provenance.
4. Create one `SurfaceDistanceBandSpec` per selected parent. Supply ordered
   positive cuts, Boolean precision, and either all original boundary edges or
   an exact subset of original exterior/hole segments. The required
   `source_polygon_id` argument is the actual polygon ID for polygon-backed
   parents. For an entity-only parent with no polygon provenance, pass explicit
   `None`; the source entity must still own that parent. Do not invent a polygon
   ID. Port-split walls retain the unsplit original boundary as the distance
   origin while child regions are clipped from the parent; split seams are not
   inset origins.
5. Call `plan.set_surface_distance_bands(...)`, then prepare again to obtain
   `snapshot1 = plan.prepare()`.
6. Give that snapshot to the Palace simulation with `sim.set_plan(snapshot1)`
   and configure the EPR request. Choose mesh and numerical controls before
   building the mesh and writing config. The plan owns its vacuum region, so do
   not add a second simulation airbox. The partition is planar polygon
   geometry; the [GeometryPlan contract](../geometry-sgb.qmd#surface-distance-bands)
   covers source identity, edge selection and precision.

## Choose mesh sizing

The shared `size_policy` selects how Gmsh chooses element sizes. To use its
native sizing while keeping the Delaunay 3D algorithm, call:

```python
sim.set_mesh(size_policy="gmsh_default", algorithm_3d="Delaunay")
```

For this example, select the Eigenmode AMR settings before writing config:

```python
sim.set_numerical(
    amr_nonconformal=True,
    amr_max_passes=20,
    amr_tolerance=0.02,
    amr_update_fraction=0.7,
)
```

Those values are caller choices for this example, not library defaults or
adequacy criteria. A positive pass limit requires both tolerance and update
fraction. Later calls may omit these controls to retain the selected values;
`amr_max_passes=0` disables adaptive refinement and allows tolerance and update
fraction to remain unset. Mesh sizing does not change physical groups,
junctions or the surface-band partition. Palace band totals are direct EPR
contributions; no Q2D factor is applied. The `0.5 µm` and `1 µm` cuts partition
the geometry into adjacent intervals, while the returned cutoff totals are
cumulative tails (`distance >= cutoff`). The `0.5 µm` total includes the
`1 µm` total, so do not add the two values. See the shared
[Palace mesh-size policy](../specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#palace-mesh-size-policy)
for defaults, state transitions and retained mesh evidence.

After setting these controls, call `sim.mesh()` and `sim.write_config()` before
preparing the Palace handoff.

## Prepare and read the Palace result

Configure Palace EPR from the same source geometry and prepare its handoff
using the mesh and config above. Run the handoff as a separate action with the
supported Palace executable. The geometry-band entries use the official
Palace 0.18.1 surface-EPR path. For solver setup, handoff and return reading,
see the [Palace Eigenmode course](palace-eigenmode.qmd).

After `resolve_palace_result` returns a `ResolvedPalaceResult`, select a native
iteration number from its retained return receipt or native metadata; there
is no iteration-discovery function. The public readers are:

```python
from scgsim.palace.results import SurfaceBandSelection, aggregate_surface_bands
from scgsim.palace.results.epr import epr_result
```

Read the selected iteration with `epr_result(resolved,
palace_iteration=iteration)`. Build one
`SurfaceBandSelection(parent_surface_id, interface_kind, field_side)` for each
selected parent using its source-bound catalogue row and matching
`construction.surfaces` metadata. Pass those selections, the selected mode,
`palace_iteration=iteration`, and `cutoffs_um=(0.5, 1.0)` to
`aggregate_surface_bands(...)`. Each cutoff must match a declared source-band
boundary, and the selected parent must have its complete recorded band and
component inventory. The result is a `PalaceSurfaceBandTotals` value that can
be retained with `to_payload()`.

For three selected interfaces it contains six cumulative cutoff totals. Each
value records its source parent, mode, native iteration, interface, cutoff and
normalization. The `>= 0.5 µm` value includes the `>= 1 µm` value; do not add
them. This offline aggregation reads existing Palace results and does not run
Palace or apply a Q2D correction.

Previously saved native mask-margin results remain readable in their historical
format; the current producer rejects non-empty `inset_margins_um`. The pinned
[SimplePad SurfaceBands workflow](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/d413d04565b3ff6946fd8b6ef237283dc187e552/notebooks/src/SCGSimExamples/SurfaceBands/SimplePad/palace_eigenmode_bands.qmd)
and [shared interface model](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/d413d04565b3ff6946fd8b6ef237283dc187e552/notebooks/src/SCGSimExamples/SurfaceBands/SimplePad/simplepad_interface_model.json)
are historical references to an earlier paired-Q2D workflow. Follow the
GeometryPlan and result-reading steps on this page for the current Palace-only
band workflow.
